create.name: Kristi Nelson
create.bio:
Kristi Nelson teaches gratefulness as a spiritual practice: the habit of meeting each day, including the hard ones, as an unearned gift. From 2014 to 2023 she led A Network for Grateful Living, the nonprofit that grew from Brother David Steindl-Rast's teaching on gratefulness, and she still serves as one of its ambassadors. Before that she spent decades helping organisations working for social and spiritual change, among them the Center for Contemplative Mind in Society, the Buddhist Peace Fellowship and the Institute for Jewish Spirituality. With Lynne Twist she set up the Soul of Money Institute as its first director, and she once raised funds for Kripalu itself. She holds a public administration master's from Harvard.

Her book Wake Up Grateful sets out a practice built on a few simple principles, such as treating life as a gift and noticing that the ordinary is extraordinary, and works through ten areas of life with reflections and exercises. A long experience of serious illness shapes her view that no day should be taken for granted. She now teaches through workshops, talks, readings, podcasts and writing, with a growing focus on growing older gratefully, and lives among farmland in western Massachusetts.

books.title: Wake Up Grateful: The Transformative Practice of Taking Nothing for Granted
books.author: Kristi Nelson
books.description: Her guide to making gratefulness a daily way of being rather than an occasional feeling. Drawing on her own life and her years at A Network for Grateful Living, it offers principles, questions, affirmations and exercises across ten areas of life. Foreword by Brother David Steindl-Rast.

courses.title: Aging Gratefully: The Power of Appreciative Presence
courses.description: A weekend at Kripalu on meeting the years ahead with appreciation rather than resistance. Short meditations, poetry, reflective writing, paired conversation and practical exercises help participants look at what growing older makes possible and how to stay present with the unknown.

free_resources.title: Meditations on Five Grateful Living Principles
free_resources.description: Five short guided video meditations on her site, one for each of the principles she teaches, from seeing life as a gift and welcoming surprise to finding wonder in ordinary things and letting appreciation and love change you.

sprint.tier_evidence: Instagram @gratefulkristi 132 (og:description, 1 Nov 2026); Facebook /gratefulkristi 69 (og:description, 1 Nov 2026); no own YouTube, X or TikTok found → ~200 total → local_hero
flags: Her story centres on surviving stage IV cancer (site, Kripalu page, book blurbs). The bio refers only to 'a long experience of serious illness' and no item makes a health claim; the Kripalu page mentions it in passing. A human may prefer to drop the illness reference from the bio.

Gratitude teacher, author and former nonprofit director rather than a lineage-based spiritual teacher; her work is framed as spiritual practice (gratefulness, Brother David Steindl-Rast), so not skipped.
All five videos are interviews or talks on other channels where she is the main speaker; she has no YouTube channel of her own.
Availability worldwide: she lives in western Massachusetts but has no base where she holds classes; she teaches through workshops at venues, talks and podcasts.

Possible overlap with A Network for Grateful Living (gratefulness.org) if that organisation is ever listed; she led it 2014-2023. Her old address kristi@gratefulness.org appears in her site's code but the published contact is grateful@kristinelson.net (mailto on every page).
Thin listing (5 videos, 1 book, 1 offering, 1 free resource) but above the threshold.
One photo only: Kripalu's full-size headshot file (the image on her own site is a landscape).
left_out: The Gratitude Explorer Workbook (ISBN 1635862067): amazon.com /dp/ returned 500 to curl and WebFetch, so not verified.
Everyday Gratitude (A Network for Grateful Living): she wrote only the introduction.
Videos on chronic illness channels ('Living Beyond Diagnosis', 'Gratefully Living the Chronic Life', 'The Power of Life Saving Gratitude') and the NEPM 'Kristi Nelson' feature: health framing.
Short publisher clips under ~3 minutes and Spanish-language Sube la Vibra clips: promotional or very short.
Workshops, speaking and readings: booked via contact form, no public page or price.
